definitions.body_md: Fix the finite universe $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, input $x$, input baseline vector $r$, and a real-valued model $v$. results.original_proof_md:
Appendix F, physical PDF page 15. Complete author mathematical proof transcription of Theorem 3.3; errors are retained. Equation numbers refer to the formal PDF.

The statement (14) specifies $I_{and}(\varnothing\mid x)=v_{and}(x_\varnothing)=v(x_\varnothing)$ and $I_{or}(\varnothing\mid x)=v_{or}(x_\varnothing)=0$, and asserts
\[
v(x_T)=v_{and}(x_T)+v_{or}(x_T)
=\sum_{S\subseteq T}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)+\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T).
\]
The complete AND calculation (15) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{S\subseteq T}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)
&=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\sum_{L\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|L|}v_{and}(x_L)\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}\sum_{S:L\subseteq S\subseteq T}(-1)^{|S|-|L|}v_{and}(x_L)\\
&=v_{and}(x_T)+\sum_{L\subseteq T,L\ne T}v_{and}(x_L)\underbrace{\sum_{m=0}^{|T|-|L|}(-1)^m}_{\text{source labels this }0}\\
&=v_{and}(x_T).
\end{aligned}
\]
The printed inner sum omits the binomial multiplicity. The complete OR calculation (16), using the source's $S_1,S_2$ grouping, is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T)
&=-\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing,S\ne\varnothing}\sum_{L\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|L|}v_{or}(x_{N\setminus L})\\
&=-\sum_{L\subseteq N}\sum_{S:S\cap T\ne\varnothing,\,S\supseteq L}(-1)^{|S|-|L|}v_{or}(x_{N\setminus L})\\
&=-v_{or}(x_\varnothing)-v_{or}(x_T)\underbrace{\sum_{|S_2|=1}^{|T|}\binom{|T|}{|S_2|}(-1)^{|S_2|}}_{\text{source labels }-1}\\
&\quad-\sum_{L\cap T\ne\varnothing,L\ne N}v_{or}(x_{N\setminus L})
\underbrace{\sum_{S_1\subseteq N\setminus T\setminus L}\sum_{|S_2|=|T\cap L|}^{|T|}
\binom{|T|-|T\cap L|}{|S_2|-|T\cap L|}(-1)^{|S_1|+|S_2|}}_{\text{source labels }0}\\
&\quad-\sum_{L\cap T=\varnothing,L\ne N\setminus T}v_{or}(x_{N\setminus L})
\underbrace{\sum_{S_2\subsetneq T}\sum_{S_1\subseteq N\setminus T\setminus L}(-1)^{|S_1|+|S_2|}}_{\text{source labels }0}\\
&=v_{or}(x_T)-v_{or}(x_\varnothing).
\end{aligned}
\]
The isolated first two terms are labeled $L=N$ and $L=N\setminus T$. Thus the source states $v_{or}(x_T)=\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S)+v_{or}(x_\varnothing)$.

The final calculation (17) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
v(x_T)&=v_{and}(x_T)+v_{or}(x_T)\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq T}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)+\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing,S\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T)+v_{or}(x_\varnothing)\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq T,S\ne\varnothing}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)+v_{and}(x_\varnothing)+\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T)+v_{or}(x_\varnothing)\\
&=v(x_\varnothing)+\sum_{S\subseteq T,S\ne\varnothing}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)+\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T)\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq T}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)+\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T).
\end{aligned}
\]
The author concludes the theorem. The fixed original-game values in the source expansion and its $x_T$ coefficient labels are independently distinguished in the project rewrite.

en.title: Theorem 3.3: universal AND/OR matching
en.overview: Reconstruct the AND and OR components by Möbius inversion, checking both the source’s conditional form and the fixed form without interchanging their OR coefficients.
assumptions: $T\subseteq N$; the source theorem stipulates $a(\varnothing)=b$, $o(\varnothing)=0$, equivalently $\gamma_\varnothing=b/2$.

definitions.body_md: Fix finite $N$, input $x$, and input baseline $r$; $g(U)=v(x_U)$ and $b=g(\varnothing)$. Write $a=g_{and}=g/2+\gamma$, $o=g_{or}=g/2-\gamma$, $A=I_{g_{and}}$ for the Möbius dividend, and $O=O_{g_{or}}$ for the nonempty negative complementary dividend. Total-output and component dividends have distinct scopes.

Read the source conditioning on $x_T$ as repeated masking: $g_T(U)=g(T\cap U)$ and $\gamma_T(U)=\gamma(T\cap U)$, with similarly restricted components $a_T,o_T$. Put $A_T=I_{a_T}$ and, for nonempty $S$, $O_T(S)=-I_{U\mapsto o_T(N\setminus U)}(S)$. The same split is restricted along the mask; independently relearning it defines another instance.

proof_steps.title: Reconstruct AND with the missing binomial counts
proof_steps.body_md: For any finite game $a$, exchanging finite sums gives $\sum_{S\subseteq T}A(S)=\sum_{L\subseteq T}a(L)\sum_{U\subseteq T\setminus L}(-1)^{|U|}=a(T)$. Each size $j$ occurs $\binom{|T|-|L|}{j}$ times, so the binomial theorem cancels the inner sum. Eq.(15) omits this coefficient; the project restores it for the same claim.

proof_steps.title: Reconstruct OR by complementary inversion
proof_steps.body_md:
Set $h(U)=o(N\setminus U)$. Möbius inversion gives $\sum_{S\subseteq N,S
e\varnothing}O(S)=o(N)-o(\varnothing)$ and $\sum_{S\subseteq N\setminus T,S
e\varnothing}O(S)=o(N)-o(T)$. Subtracting retains exactly the sets meeting $T$, yielding $\sum_{S\cap T
e\varnothing}O(S)=o(T)-o(\varnothing)$. This full cancellation also avoids Eq.(16)’s printed signs: because its $S_2$ contains $T\cap L$, the exponent must subtract $|T\cap L|$, which the source omits. A zero-factor proof must check both remaining blocks, rather than just one.

proof_steps.title: Combine the fixed and conditional games
proof_steps.body_md: The fixed formula follows from $a+o=g$ and $o(\varnothing)=0$. Apply the same inversion to $g_T$ and the restricted split: $g_T(T)=g(T)$, $a_T(\varnothing)=b$, and $o_T(\varnothing)=0$, which gives the source’s conditional formula. If $S\subseteq T$, then $A_T(S)=A(S)$ because every subcoalition $U$ satisfies $T\cap U=U$. OR complementary terms generally differ and cannot be replaced by the same argument. If a free split is independently relearned for $x_T$, apply the same reconstruction theorem directly to that new split and check its stated empty convention; the new optimizer need not equal the old $\gamma$ restricted to the mask. The current conditional declaration encodes restriction of a fixed split, whereas base and_or_matching can be separately instantiated with the new split.

results.original_proof_md:
Appendix G, physical PDF page 16. Complete author mathematical proof transcription of Lemma 3.4, including its external-reference argument and the duplicate-baseline equality.

The statement (18) says that every masked output can be universally matched by a small set of salient interactions:
\[
\begin{aligned}
v(x_T)&=v_{and}(x_T)+v_{or}(x_T)
=\sum_{S\subseteq T}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)+\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T)\\
&\approx v(x_\varnothing)
+\sum_{S\in\Omega_{salient}^{and}:\varnothing\ne S\subseteq T}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)
+\sum_{S\in\Omega_{salient}^{or}:S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T).
\end{aligned}
\]
The entire author argument first cites Ren et al. (2023a) for the claim that, under common conditions (footnote 1), a well-trained DNN output $v_{and}(x_T)$ on all $2^n$ masks is approximated by a small number of AND interactions with salient effects, with $|\Omega_{salient}^{and}|\ll2^n$.

It then invokes Appendix C's assertion that OR interactions are particular AND interactions, and concludes that a well-trained DNN output $v_{or}(x_T)$ is similarly approximated by a small number of OR interactions, with $|\Omega_{salient}^{or}|\ll2^n$.

The final calculation (19), retained exactly in its baseline placement, is
\[
\begin{aligned}
v(x_T)&=v_{and}(x_T)+v_{or}(x_T)\\
&=v(x_\varnothing)+\sum_{S\subseteq T}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)+\sum_{S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T)\\
&\approx v(x_\varnothing)
+\sum_{S\in\Omega_{salient}^{and}:\varnothing\ne S\subseteq T}I_{and}(S\mid x_T)
+\sum_{S\in\Omega_{salient}^{or}:S\cap T\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(S\mid x_T).
\end{aligned}
\]
The author concludes that Lemma 3.4 is proved. The argument contains no quantitative definition of “small” or of the approximation error, and no demonstration that both learned decomposition components satisfy the cited DNN conditions. These gaps and the first equality's duplicate empty AND dividend are recorded separately.

definitions.body_md: Fix the finite universe $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, input $x$, input baseline vector $r$, and a real-valued model $v$. The mask $x_U$ retains coordinates in $U$ and sets the others to $r$; write $g(U)=v(x_U)$ and output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$. The source input baseline $b_i$ is distinct from this scalar $b$. Choose one decomposition function $\gamma$ and put $a(U)=g(U)/2+\gamma_U$, $o(U)=g(U)/2-\gamma_U$, so that $a+o=g$. The AND component dividend is $A(S)=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}a(U)$; the nonempty OR component dividend is $O(S)=-\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}o(N\setminus U)$. The raw total-output dividend $I_g$ and component dividend $A$ remain distinct. Local $a=g_{and}$, $o=g_{or}$, $A=I_{g_{and}}$, and $O=O_{g_{or}}$ abbreviate the corresponding public concepts.

Write $A_l(S),O_l(S)$ for the fixed sample’s component dividends at layer $l$. Order is $|S|$. Footnote 7 uses $\tau_l=0.05\max_{S}\max\{|A_l(S)|,|O_l(S)|\}$ and $\Omega_{and}^{l,m}=\{S\subseteq N:|S|=m,|A_l(S)|>\tau_l\}$, with the analogous OR family. Appendix M.4 instead uses a maximum across samples for its sparsity experiment, which is distinct from footnote 7’s sample-specific threshold. Footnote 8 divides all layer dividends by $c_l=\mathbb E_x|g_l(N)-g_l(\varnothing)|$; this is undefined when $c_l=0$. The shared coefficient $s(a,b)$ is $0$ for opposite signs and $\operatorname{sign}(a)\min(|a|,|b|)$ for the same sign, with value $0$ at a zero argument.

proof_steps.title: Retain the supports of shared and residual strengths
proof_steps.body_md: Let $s_S=s(A_l(S),A_L(S))$. In Eq.(7), overlap ranges only over the common salient support, whereas forget ranges over the entire current-layer salient support and new over the entire final-layer salient support. The latter two still subtract $s_S$ defined from the two actual coefficients; $s_S$ is not defined only on the common salient family. Replace $A,\Omega_{and}$ by $O,\Omega_{or}$ for OR metrics.

proof_steps.title: Define ratios and cross-model IoU
proof_steps.body_md: Completeness divides overlap by the final-layer all strength, and redundancy divides forget by the current-layer all strength. These are numerical metrics under the stated definitions; their names do not imply feature completeness or a generalization guarantee. IoU counts same-order coalition families and lies in $[0,1]$ when the union is nonempty; an empty union gives the source fraction $0/0$.

proof_steps.title: Define stability under genuine random noise
proof_steps.body_md: Let $\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I)$, $\mu_l(S,x)=\mathbb E_\epsilon A_l(S\mid x+\epsilon)$, and $\nu_l(S,x)=\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon A_l(S\mid x+\epsilon)$. The source first averages $|\mu_l|/\sqrt{\nu_l}$ over salient $S$ and then over samples. It does not treat layer coefficients as random noise or identify the perturbation with learned residual $\delta_T$. The relevant moments and positive variance are needed for the real fraction; no zero-variance or empty-family convention is supplied.

proof_steps.title: 明确阶乘权重与掩码边际
proof_steps.body_md: 令 $n=|N|$，$U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}$，$w(U)=|U|!(n-|U|-1)!/n!$。经典 Shapley 是 $\sum_Uw(U)[g(U\cup\{i\})-g(U)]$。固定重构式相减后，AND 项留下包含 $i$ 且其他成员都在 $U$ 的集合；OR 项留下包含 $i$ 且其他成员都不在 $U$ 的集合。基线抵消。

proof_steps.title: 按排列首尾计数均分权重
proof_steps.body_md: 均匀随机排列中，$U$ 恰为 $i$ 的前驱集的概率是 $w(U)$。固定 $S\ni i$ 时，AND 被 $i$ 激活恰当 $i$ 最后出现在 $S$ 中，OR 被 $i$ 激活恰当 $i$ 最先出现。$S$ 中各成员处于最先或最后位置的事件互斥且等概率，并覆盖全部排列，所以各概率为 $1/|S|$。这对正负系数均成立。
proof_steps.formula_tex: \mathbb P(i\text{ is last in }S)=\mathbb P(i\text{ is first in }S)=\frac1{|S|}.

proof_steps.title: 交换有限和并合成结论
proof_steps.body_md: 固定每个交互的激活概率后，交换有限交互和与排列平均，得到两种交互分别均分，合并即原式。所有被计入的 $S$ 都含 $i$，因此非空，分母正。Lean 直接走等价的阶乘权重有限和路线，核验同一最终结论，并非单独形式化本段排列叙述。

en.title: Appendix B: Shapley sharing of AND/OR dividends
en.overview: Start from the classical factorial marginal and count last/first occurrences in permutations.
assumptions: $i\in N$; a single fixed split $g=a+o$; no zero output baseline is required.

definitions.body_md: Fix finite $N$, input $x$, and input baseline $r$; $g(U)=v(x_U)$ and $b=g(\varnothing)$. Write $a=g_{and}=g/2+\gamma$, $o=g_{or}=g/2-\gamma$, $A=I_{g_{and}}$ for the Möbius dividend, and $O=O_{g_{or}}$ for the nonempty negative complementary dividend. Total-output and component dividends have distinct scopes.

proof_steps.title: Specify factorial weights and the masked marginal
proof_steps.body_md: Let $n=|N|$, $U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}$, and $w(U)=|U|!(n-|U|-1)!/n!$. Classical Shapley is $\sum_Uw(U)[g(U\cup\{i\})-g(U)]$. Subtracting the fixed reconstruction formulas retains AND coalitions containing $i$ whose other members are in $U$, and OR coalitions containing $i$ whose other members are outside $U$. The baseline cancels.

proof_steps.title: Count equal shares by first and last positions
proof_steps.body_md: In a uniform random permutation, $w(U)$ is the probability that $U$ is exactly the predecessor set of $i$. For fixed $S\ni i$, $i$ activates the AND term precisely when it is last within $S$, and activates the OR term precisely when it is first. The members’ first-position events, or last-position events, are disjoint, equiprobable, and exhaust all permutations; each has probability $1/|S|$. This counting applies to coefficients of either sign.

proof_steps.title: Exchange finite sums and combine the contributions
proof_steps.body_md: After determining each activation probability, exchange the finite dividend sum and permutation average. Both interaction types are shared equally, and adding them yields the stated formula. Every included $S$ contains $i$, so its denominator is positive. Lean uses the equivalent finite factorial-weight route to verify this final equality; it does not separately formalize the permutation narrative.

results.original_proof_md:
Appendix C, physical PDF page 13. Complete mathematical argument as printed, including the two coordinate definitions and the subsequent sparsity inference.

The source calls OR a specific AND interaction after inverting masked and unmasked states. It defines (11)
\[
(x_{N\setminus T})_i=\begin{cases}x_i&i\in N\setminus T,\\b_i&i\in T,\end{cases}
\]
then defines the supposedly inverted sample in (12) by
\[
(x'_T)_i=\begin{cases}x_i&i\in T,\\b_i&i\in N\setminus T.\end{cases}
\]
It then prints (13)
\[
I_{or}(S\mid x)=-\sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}v(x_{N\setminus T})
=-\sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}v(x'_T)
=-I_{and}(S\mid x').
\]
The concluding paragraph states that this equality transfers the proven AND sparsity of Ren et al. (2024) to OR sparsity, so most well-trained DNNs encode only a small number of OR interactions. The printed Eq.(12) is the ordinary original mask, not the coordinate-swapped mask needed for the second equality. That equality and the unsupported transfer of sparsity assumptions are treated as separate issues.

definitions.body_md: Fix the finite universe $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, input $x$, input baseline vector $r$, and a real-valued model $v$. The mask $x_U$ retains coordinates in $U$ and sets the others to $r$; write $g(U)=v(x_U)$ and output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$. The source input baseline $b_i$ is distinct from this scalar $b$. Choose one decomposition function $\gamma$ and put $a(U)=g(U)/2+\gamma_U$, $o(U)=g(U)/2-\gamma_U$, so that $a+o=g$. The AND component dividend is $A(S)=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}a(U)$; the nonempty OR component dividend is $O(S)=-\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}o(N\setminus U)$. The raw total-output dividend $I_g$ and component dividend $A$ remain distinct. Local $a=g_{and}$, $o=g_{or}$, $A=I_{g_{and}}$, and $O=O_{g_{or}}$ abbreviate the corresponding public concepts.
